## The collections

- *Mumonkan* (Chinese *Wumenguan*), the Gateless Gate, compiled in 1228 by Wumen Huikai. 48 cases, each with his comment and a verse. Short enough to carry in a coat pocket.
- *Hekiganroku*, the Blue Cliff Record, 100 cases, compiled 1125 by Yuanwu Keqin from earlier verses by Xuedou. Dense and much harder.

## Case 1: Jōshū's dog

A monk asked Zhaozhou (Jōshū in Japanese): "Does a dog have Buddha nature?" Jōshū said: "Mu." Literally "no" or "not", but the point is it is not an answer to the question. Wumen's comment tells you to hold Mu day and night "like a red-hot iron ball you have swallowed and can't spit out". That image has stayed with me since I first read it in Robert Aitken, *The Gateless Barrier* (North Point, 1990), p. 7.

## Hakuin's one hand

Hakuin Ekaku (1686 to 1769), who reformed Rinzai Zen in Japan and organised koans into a curriculum. "Two hands clap and there is a sound. What is the sound of one hand?" The pop-culture version of Zen comes almost entirely from this one. Rinzai uses koans; Sōtō mostly sits, shikantaza, "just sitting", after Dōgen.

## The sesshin, November 2024

Three days at a small zendo in Ranelagh, 15 to 17 November 2024, €140 including meals. Teacher: Máire Ní Fhloinn, who trained in Kamakura for eleven years. Up at 5:30, nine periods of 25-minute sitting a day, walking meditation in between, silence throughout. Each morning a short private interview (dokusan). I was given Mu. On day two I said something clever about negation and she rang the bell before I finished. On day three I said nothing and she smiled. I don't know what that means and suspect that's the point.

Knees: bad. Bought a proper zafu afterwards, €45. The stretches in [[朝のヨガ]] help.

## What a history teacher makes of it

The koans are also historical documents: Song dynasty monastic politics, lineages, who was claiming whose authority. Wumen was writing at a time when koan study was becoming a fixed system. Ikkyū mocked exactly that at Daitoku-ji in the 1400s, and Ikkyū is the link to tea; see [[禅と茶道]]. Walked round Daitoku-ji in April 2024; Ryōan-ji is for the next trip to [[Kyoto]].
